🤖 THREEHALVES — THE CENTAUR ROBOT Threehalves is a 7-foot-tall teleoperated robot developed by Satyress. Its design combines a human-like torso and arms with a powerful four-legged chassis, creating a mechanical centaur built for environments that are too dangerous for humans. The idea behind Threehalves is simple: instead of sending a person into extreme heat, unstable terrain, darkness, hazardous industrial environments or disaster zones, a skilled operator can control the robot remotely and perform the work from a safer location. Unlike many humanoid robots, Threehalves is designed around tools and equipment that humans already use. Its modular limbs and quick-connect system allow it to be adapted for different tasks, while its four-legged platform provides stability on difficult terrain. The most unsettling part is probably its appearance. With its enormous size, humanoid body, four mechanical legs and distinctive horned head, Threehalves looks less like a traditional industrial machine and more like something from a science-fiction horror movie. But behind the terrifying design is a serious engineering concept: putting the machine in danger instead of the human. Threehalves is still a developing robotics project, but it represents a strange glimpse into a future where dangerous jobs could be performed remotely — with a human controlling the machine from a distance. And honestly… it might be one of the creepiest robots ever built. 👁️ #threehalves #robot #baal #satyress #horrortok

Chinese humanoid robots broke records set by humans, including Usain Bolt's 100m sprint world record, on the opening day of the Olympics-like World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing on Saturday. More than 2,000 humanoid robots were participating in the event, organisers said. In a 100-metre sprint, a humanoid robot achieved a result of 9.39 seconds, beating the human record of 9.58 seconds set by Jamaican athlete Bolt in 2009. In a standing high jump, a humanoid robot was able to reach 2.88m, well above the 0.95m best result by a humanoid in last year’s first edition of the games. It surpassed the human high jump record of 2.45m set by Cuba’s Javier Sotomayor in 1993. The five-day games, now in their second year, are a spectacle demonstrating China’s rapid progress in advanced robotics as the technology race with the US heats up. There are 51 events and more than 1,000 competitions taking place, including running, table tennis and football. For more news, visit @sbsnews_au (link in bio).

China's LIFELIKE Robot Face Will Make You Question Everything #news #technology #china #robot  Chinese startup AheadForm has built a humanoid robot head that is nearly impossible to distinguish from a real human face. Powered by thirty precision brushless micro motors embedded beneath bionic silicone skin, the robot controls every blink, every glance, and every subtle micro expression with stunning accuracy. Cameras integrated directly into the eyes allow the robot to track faces in real time, while an onboard AI system reads human emotions and responds instantly with matching expressions. This is not a CGI render or a movie prop. This is real technology being developed right now in China for deployment in customer service, healthcare, and personal companionship. A viral video of the robot posted in March 2026 reignited a global conversation about whether hyper realistic robot faces are the missing key to making humanoid robots commercially successful. AheadForm believes the future of human robot interaction depends not just on what robots can do, but on how real they feel. The face of the future just got a lot harder to spot.

Vitarobotics, humanoid robot, bionic robot, embodied AI et robotics intégrés naturellement. Vitarobotics is building one of the most human-shaped robots coming out of China right now. This video shows a Vitarobotics bionic humanoid prototype lying on a workbench while its lower body changes position. The hips and knees move through large angles, both legs lift independently, and the robot holds several human-like poses. Part of the outer shell is open, so you can also see the internal cables and mechanical structure underneath. Vitarobotics, also known as 维塔智能机器人, develops high-realism bionic service robots for areas including reception, tourism, live streaming, commercial displays and human interaction.  According to its AGIC 2026 exhibitor information, the company’s full bionic humanoid platform uses 46 axes, with 23 for the body and 23 for the head. Vitarobotics also describes flexible tactile skin across the body, touch-responsive movements, facial micro-expression control and a temperature-controlled skin system.  The exposed mechanical layout is the part I kept looking at. The hip and leg movements show how many moving components have to fit inside a body designed around human proportions. Vitarobotics presented its bionic humanoid robots at AGIC 2026 in Shenzhen, China.  #Vitarobotics #HumanoidRobot #Robotics #EmbodiedAI #BionicRobot

Hugging Face and its Pollen Robotics subsidiary have opened preorders for Microduck, a $399 desktop-sized robot built for experimenting with “physical AI.”  The 25cm robot contains 15 motors, a camera, a depth sensor, two inertial measurement units, and a “beak” that can grasp small objects.  Its open-source software allows developers to train behaviors through reinforcement learning in a physics simulator before transferring them to the real machine.  Microduck can already walk, crouch, follow a laser, grab objects, and recover from many falls.  More than 10,000 units were preordered in its first five days, roughly $4 million! Initial deliveries are targeted before Christmas of this year in North America, Europe, and the UK. Would you buy one?

Figure did something absolutely wild with its retired humanoid robots. 🤯🔥 Instead of dismantling its F.02 fleet, Figure trained the robots to autonomously jump into a 75-ton electric arc furnace filled with molten steel in Imatra, Finland. And yes this was real. Figure says the robots were: 🤖 Trained to jump in simulation 🦘 Practiced with airbags at its San Jose campus 🏭 Sent to a foundry the team had never visited 🔥 Given only six furnace melts across 24 hours ⚡ Operating despite extreme heat and electromagnetic interference The reason? Figure wanted to decommission the F.02 fleet while protecting proprietary hardware and freeing engineering resources for its next-generation robots. The resulting metal bars are being turned into a limited series of F.02 commemorative artifacts. And there is a serious robotics story behind the crazy video: Figure had to train a jump policy that could transfer from simulation to a completely unfamiliar real-world environment and accurately land the robot in the furnace. Arnold Schwarzenegger was also involved after suggesting the robots should be melted an obvious nod to Terminator 2. This may be the most brutal robot retirement ever. 😅 Would you call this engineering genius or the most extreme robot disposal method ever? 👀 🏢 Company: Figure , Brett Adcock ⚠️ This content is shared for informational purposes only. You can now buy a humanoid robot for $4K Humanoid robots just got insanely cheap, and this might change everything. In this video, we break down how Unitree Robotics just launched a $4,000 humanoid robot on AliExpress, a price point that was unthinkable just a few years ago. The R1 robot stands 123cm tall and can perform advanced movements like cartwheels, running downhill, and getting back up on its own. What’s wild? Robots with similar capabilities used to cost anywhere from $50,000 to $150,000, meaning prices have dropped by over 90%. Even more surprising, China is already dominating the humanoid robotics race. While companies like Tesla, Figure AI, and Agility Robotics have only shipped around 150 units each, Unitree has already shipped over 5,500 robots. What used to live in research labs and sci-fi movies is now available to anyone with a credit card, on the same platform you would use to buy everyday gadgets. I spent days teaching a 3D-printed robot duck to walk. Most of that time, it was falling over. It’s my own build of the Open Duck Mini. The open-source, BDX-inspired biped created by Antoine Pirrone. The whole thing is 3D-printed and runs on hobby-grade servos instead of industrial actuators, which is what makes it buildable on a normal budget and also what makes it so hard to get walking. The hard part wasn’t the printing or the assembly. It was the sim-to-real gap. A gait that walks perfectly in MuJoCo hits real-world joint slop, servo lag, and a center of mass that won’t sit still, and just before you know it, the duck face plants into the floor. It took me 40+ calibration passes before it could take three steps without tipping! What the build came down to: • 3D-printed chassis • Per-joint offset calibration (where most of the pain lived) • Policy training in simulation (MuJoCo / Isaac Lab) • Build guide + docs via Tnkr • A lot of failed walks Real hardware. Real failures. Real progress.

Figure just retired its old robots by training them to jump into molten steel. 🔥🤖 F.02 helped build 30,000+ BMWs. Taking each one apart by hand would have slowed down F.04, so Figure's CEO asked the internet for ideas.  Arnold Schwarzenegger replied: "You should melt them." Foundries in the US and Mexico said no because of the batteries, so they went to Finland: a 75-ton arc furnace, six melts in 24 hours, and a 20-minute window before the steel crusts over. Figure says the jumps were real and autonomous, trained in San Jose on airbags. The metal is coming back as collectible F.02 heads. Peak marketing, or a smart way to retire a fleet? 👇 Footage: Figure #bmw #robots #robotics  #ai
